name: – Raphaël Glucksmann – Commission proposal
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the screening of foreign investments in the Union and repealing Regulation (EU) 2019/452 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to rewrite the EU's rules on foreign investment screening. Every EU country would have to check foreign takeovers and new foreign-built facilities in sensitive areas, such as ports, energy grids, chip factories, hospitals and media. Countries would share information and the Commission could give opinions, and in some disputed cases take the final decision. The aim is to protect security and public order while keeping Europe open to investment.

- All EU countries must screen foreign investments in sensitive sectors, with common deadlines and a single EU filing portal.
- It affects foreign investors, EU companies being bought, and national authorities; the Commission gets stronger powers.
- Parliament adopted its position; talks with EU governments on the final law come next.
